repo_standards_ref: estimate_batch.py / estimate_store.py sibling-module conventions (the handoff's named pattern reference); references/global-crew.md; g1/g2 frozen record shape

smells.finding: run_grip_batch is ~33 lines of clear nested season->GP->session loop; get_grip_at body is ~25 lines mostly a documented delta-method formula. Neither is a long-method smell.
No class added except the trivial GripRecordNotFoundError exception (docstring only).
run_grip_batch intentionally mirrors estimate_batch.py's cross-module pattern, but that is not in-diff copy-paste duplication; error-handling and upsert paths each appear once.

get_grip_at is a module-level function using GripStore's PUBLIC load() API (not reaching into internals) -- consistent with error_record also being a free function alongside GripStore. The load-all-then-pandas-filter cost is a separately-flagged perf triage (#2), not envy.
(year, gp_name, session_type) travels together as the PK triple across run_grip_batch/get_grip_at/error_record/fit signatures.

override.repo_standard: estimate_store.py / estimate_batch.py / grip_baseline.py (g2) all pass (year, gp_name, session_type) as separate positional params; g1 froze the PK as the _PK tuple and the GripEstimateRecord field order; the handoff's explicit constraint is 'mirror estimate_batch.py's pattern exactly'.
override.reason: Introducing a PK value-object here would diverge this one module from every sibling in layer2 and break the deliberate estimate_batch.py mirroring the handoff mandates -- the documented sibling-module convention subordinates the clump.

smells.finding: The -1 error sentinel is a named module constant (_UNKNOWN_SESSION_ID) with an explanatory comment, not a bare magic literal.
run_grip_batch takes 9 params (store + 8 keyword-only: seasons, db_path, force, session_type, fit_fn, calendar_fn, record_fn, log).

override.repo_standard: The handoff's non-negotiable constraint is 'Mirror estimate_batch.py's injectable-collaborator-fn seam exactly' -- run_estimate_batch has the same shape; each fn param is a genuine test seam exercised by the injected-fake unit tests.
override.reason: The injectable-seam pattern is the explicitly required design (it is what lets tests fake DB/fit without touching real FastF1); collapsing it into a config object would defeat the mandated seam and diverge from the sibling driver.

smells.finding: New sibling module; no cross-cutting edit rippled across many files.
grip_batch.py has one reason to change (batch orchestration); get_grip_at has one (consumer curve evaluation).
No train-wreck chains; store.load(...) then a single pandas filter.
record_fn/fit_fn/calendar_fn are all real, tested seams (isolation tests drive the record_fn path); no unused hooks or hypothetical extension points.

The module/function docstrings explain genuine design decisions (record_fn re-mapping vs estimate_batch's split, the -1 sentinel, the dropped rate cross-terms in the delta-method) -- they document real choices, they do not paper over unclear code.
